theme: What 25,000 Participants Taught Us About Human ROI

linkedin.text:
A sales director said something to us at the end of a 5-day incentive program that I still think about.

She said: "I've managed this team for four years. I understood more about how they work, what drives them, and where the friction actually is — in five days here than in all of that time combined."

She wasn't describing a team-building session.
She was describing what changes when you take the same people, remove the org chart, and put them inside an experience that's genuinely worth sharing.

After 25,000+ participants across 130+ destinations and 16 years of corporate event production, this is the pattern that repeats:

The measurable ROI of incentive travel — retention lift, quota attainment, engagement scores — is real. But the harder-to-quantify ROI is the interpersonal capital that accumulates when people experience something together outside the office.

For HR and sales leaders managing high-performance teams: how do you currently measure the relational outcomes of off-site experiences — and is that showing up in your program design decisions?

Genuinely interested in how others are approaching this.
